name: EPHB4-related lymphatic-related hydrops fetalis
aliases: Lymphatic dysplasia with hydrops fetalis due to EPHB4 mutation

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in the EPHB4 gene
Presence of non-immune hydrops fetalis detected prenatally by ultrasound
Evidence of lymphatic dysplasia or malformations on imaging or histopathology
Family history of hydrops fetalis or lymphatic anomalies consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of prenatal hydrops fetalis and lymphatic malformations with confirmed pathogenic EPHB4 variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic testing combined with prenatal imaging findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Generalized fetal edema without evidence of red cell alloimmunization
searchTerms: severe fetal swelling not caused by immune issues

pathognomonic.notes: Abnormal development of lymphatic vessels leading to fluid accumulation
Accumulation of lymphatic fluid in the pleural cavity

common.notes: Fluid accumulation in the pleural space detected prenatally or postnatally
Reduced fetal size compared to gestational age
searchTerms: baby smaller than expected in womb

occasional.notes: Swelling of the skin due to lymphatic fluid accumulation
Lymphatic fluid accumulation in the peritoneal cavity
Reduced hemoglobin levels without evidence of hemolysis

rare.notes: Pleural effusion lacking lymphatic fluid characteristics
searchTerms: fluid in chest cavity without chyle

rare.notes: Non-specific minor heart defects occasionally reported

laboratory: Normal or mildly decreased hemoglobin and platelet counts
Absence of red cell alloimmunization markers
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing generalized fetal edema (hydrops fetalis)
Pleural, pericardial effusions and ascites on fetal imaging
Lymphatic vessel abnormalities on specialized imaging (e.g., fetal MRI, lymphoscintigraphy)
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Histopathological confirmation of lymphatic dysplasia in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Hydrops caused by a variety of genetic, infectious, or hematologic etiologies
May present with hydrops but often with additional systemic features
Different genetic causes such as CCBE1 or PIEZO1 mutations

redFlags: Severe non-immune hydrops fetalis detected prenatally
Rapidly progressive pleural effusions causing respiratory compromise
Family history of unexplained fetal demise or hydrops
references: Orphanet: EPHB4-related lymphatic-related hydrops fetalis, ORPHA:568065
Brouillard P, et al. EPHB4 mutations cause autosomal dominant lymphatic-related hydrops fetalis. J Med Genet. 2017.
Lymphatic Malformations and Hydrops Fetalis: Clinical and Genetic Insights. Prenat Diagn. 2020.
